players.product: GEM 63 / GEM 63XL solid rocket boosters for the Atlas V and Vulcan launch vehicles

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Kathy Warden on munitions: Northrop has completed PAC-3 solid rocket motor qualification, is ramping production toward increasingly higher delivery targets and is 'far along in discussions with Lockheed Martin as to being a solid rocket motor provider for a portion of their buy' while negotiating the contract; the munitions acceleration covers '10 agreements about eight weapons' in active discussion with various primes, where Northrop supplies solid rocket motors and also seekers, cases, nozzles and fuses. Investing ahead of contract since the 2019 Orbital ATK acquisition, it has 'built two additional plants where we can build solid rocket motors' and has 'two others that are nearing completion', which it expects to let it gain share over the next couple of years.
quarterly_data.figure: 10 agreements on eight weapons; two additional SRM plants built, two more nearing completion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Kathy Warden on Sentinel: 'just this week we showed all of the missile stacked' - all missile components are built and integrated for the first time - with the first test planned in 2027, 'earlier than was anticipated'; silo construction and command and control are also progressing, with production in the 2030s after development and testing.
quarterly_data.figure: first Sentinel missile test planned in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Kathy Warden on Aeronautics: Northrop is facilitizing to build the B-21 at the faster rate agreed with the Air Force earlier this year, has started low rate initial production, and expects the Air Force to share its program-of-record conclusions with Congress later this year; the higher-than-anticipated Aeronautics margins this year come mainly from mature production programs, with B-21 in line with its estimate at completion, and she expects them to remain a tailwind in the second half. Portfolio-wide net EAC adjustments are positive, and she is 'feeling good' about the GEM 63XL and SiAW programs after the quarter's charges.

CEO Kathy Warden: the marine nuclear-submarine propulsion business is over $1 billion today and a key growth driver as submarine production scales over the next decade - Northrop is increasing its production rate to keep pace with the shipbuilders, which she described as 'basically doubling'. Mission Systems, a product-line business that is often a supplier rather than a prime, is Northrop's highest-margin and highest-return-on-capital segment and receives the most R&D, often with partners.
quarterly_data.figure: marine propulsion business over $1 billion; production rate basically doubling

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Kathy Warden on Golden Dome and funding: Northrop's Golden Dome contribution includes hot production lines such as IBCS fire control and the G/ATOR radar developed for the Marine Corps (adding quantities toward initial operating capability by 2028), missile-tracking and missile-warning satellites, the Glide Phase Interceptor in development, and space-based interceptors (development phase); national security space is growing double digits, with space resiliency and space superiority the fastest-growing portfolios. Northrop's programs are fully funded in the base budget, reconciliation is largely upside, and despite a likely extended continuing resolution it has the funding to continue work into early next year. International sales could exceed the $10 billion 2031 target, led by tactical missiles and ammunition (including counter-UAS), command and control, and international orders extending E-2D and Triton production; capex stays elevated around 4.5% of sales over the next couple of years.
quarterly_data.figure: Golden Dome initial operating capability by 2028; international target $10 billion by 2031 could be exceeded; capex around 4.5% of sales
